question: Find a single discount equivalent to successive discounts of 20%, 25% and 15%.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the given discount percentages into fraction multipliers: 20% = 4/5, 25% = 3/4, and 15% = 17/20.

Find the combined multiplier: (4/5) × (3/4) × (17/20) = 51/100.

This means the Final Selling Price is 51% of the Marked Price.

Equivalent Discount = 100% − 51% = 49%.

**∴ The correct answer is 49%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Three successive discounts of 20%, 25%, and 15%.

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (100 − D₁)/100 × (100 − D₂)/100 × ...

Discount % = [(MP − SP) / MP] × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Marked Price (MP) = 100.

⇒ Price after 1st discount of 20% = 100 − 20 = 80

⇒ Price after 2ⁿd discount of 25% = 80 − (25% of 80) = 80 − 20 = 60

⇒ Price after 3rd discount of 15% = 60 − (15% of 60) = 60 − 9 = 51

⇒ Final Selling Price (SP) = 51

⇒ Total Equivalent Discount = MP − SP = 100 − 51 = 49

⇒ Since the base MP is 100, the equivalent discount % = 49%.

**∴ The correct answer is 49%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the equivalent single discount can be directly calculated using the formula: [a + b − (a × b) / 100]%.

Marked Price (MP) vs Selling Price (SP)

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (or list price) of the item. Profit or loss, on the other hand, is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP).

Buy X Get Y Free Offers

In promotional offers, the effective discount percentage is calculated as: [Free Items ÷ Total Items] × 100.
